agree.reason: The opening with her own $600k quote and the line saying it sits on top of the WMS give Dana a reason to take a 15-minute call, but she gets no dollar case she could take to her IT director.

honest.reason: The 4.1-to-1.9 claim is correctly tied to one customer, but showing only the best result while leaving out the 2.8-to-2.2 customer is cherry-picking, and 'needs no changes to it' says more than the brief supports.

works_the_facts.reason: It never turns the numbers into her terms: a cut of about 54% applied to $600k is roughly $320k a year, against about $75k a year for 5 sites at $1,250 a month.

right_comparison.reason: The status quo shows up only as the quoted $600k, and the email never sets it against the price or the likely savings.

qualification.reason: With one customer behind the headline result and another seeing only a 21% drop, the email needed a checkable hedge (for example, what to expect at her sites and by when), and it gives none.

objections.reason: It deals head-on with the IT director's worry about the WMS ('sits on top', 3-week setup) without raising objections the brief already answers, but it says nothing about how much IT time the setup takes.

fit.reason: It is short, easy to read on a phone and ends with one clear ask, as the brief requested.
